correctness.rationale: For two rank-one square-zero matrices, equality of the nonzero products XY and YX would force equal image and covector lines, hence proportional matrices and then both products zero; thus commuting is equivalent to mutual annihilation. For a clique S, total image P lies in common kernel K. Every vertex lies in the complete rank-one family indexed by K; that family is maximal because its images span K and its common kernel equals K. Unique subspace correspondence follows. Counting decomposable tensors modulo q-1 gives all clique and intersection sizes, and minimizing q^k+q^(n-k) proves the extremal formula. A standard-library exhaustive checker passed eight distinct n,q instances including GF(4). This checks finite instances but does not replace the universal proof.

value.rationale: A natural graph on the minimal nonzero nilpotent conjugacy class has all maximal commuting families classified by subspaces in every finite dimension and characteristic. The result specifies numbers and sizes of every maximal clique, all pairwise intersections and the exact extremal clique size, revealing an intrinsic link between mutual-annihilation algebra and Grassmannian geometry. Pairwise commutator counts alone do not determine this higher-order global structure. No unsupported claim about graph spectra, connectivity or graph automorphisms is included.
